Use the long axis to organize the split and maintain a clear neighborhood-scale street building orientation.
Introduce a modest gap to create a legible void without fragmenting the building into separate objects.
Keep a grounded connecting spine so the threshold remains continuous and programmatically anchored.
Add an access-side notch to convert the frontage into an active public entry zone.

Reduce curvature so the primary mass stays calm and less sculptural, improving program legibility.
Simplify the bent mass so the form reads as one dominant gesture rather than a faceted object.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent single mass across views, so it clears basic unity and repair integrity, but it reads as a compact faceted object rather than a neighborhood living building with an active ground threshold. The parcel response is only partial: the mass sits within the boundary, yet the dominant gesture does not strongly organize itself around the site’s long/short axes or the visible access edge. The blue frontage is answered weakly; there is no clear public void, entry seam, or undercut that makes the access side legible, so the ground condition feels sealed. The silhouette is acceptable as a continuous mass, but the section does not reveal enough program-specific public/private hierarchy or terrace/court behavior to satisfy the brief. The references suggest that a prismatic object and a layered void could be useful, but the candidate currently underuses those principles. It therefore fails program_fit_hard_pass on semantic grounds, primarily due to insufficient public threshold and weak section/program expression rather than geometric incoherence.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact prismatic mixed-use object can be legible when its base and upper mass read as one coherent civic volume.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Courtyard/open-air domestic-commercial atmospheres can support a neighborhood program when the ground plane stays porous and social.
